one_sentence: This document catalogs 23 articles in Part XVI of the Theophysics Research Initiative, each deriving theological claims from physical principles.
executive_summary: This document is an index of 23 articles forming Part XVI of the Theophysics Research Initiative. The core claim is that theological concepts—such as the character of God, the nature of the adversary, salvation, grace, heaven and hell, the Trinity, and the Logos—can be rigorously derived from physical laws and mathematical structures. Key evidence includes references to specific physical forces, entropy, dynamical systems, quantum mechanics, and information theory. The conclusion is that theology and physics converge on a unified framework, with each article exploring a distinct facet of this isomorphism.
short_summary: This document is an index of 23 articles in Part XVI of the Theophysics Research Initiative. The core structural claim is that theological doctrines can be derived from physical principles and mathematical laws. Key evidence includes references to 10 physical forces, entropy, quantum mechanics, and information theory. This matters because it presents a systematic, evidence-based approach to theology grounded in physics.
